01.intro: Learning. Topics assigned by my mentor, and a UXplore session for the UX team.

sec.head: 1.1 Trust in AI
sec.sub: Research, product exploration and interaction-flow design

sec.title: Trust in AI
pts: Step 1. Understanding the problem: Explored what trust means in AI. Investigated factors that make people trust or distrust AI.

Step 2. Existing product exploration: Examined how ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini respond to user questions. Explored trust mechanisms and interactions that can change a user's confidence in an AI product.
Step 3. Designing for appropriate trust: Developed a flow exploring how an AI experience could communicate reliability and support user judgment.

Step 4. Trust and control exploration: Explored how much supporting reference information is sufficient, and when it becomes excessive. Considered what should happen when AI provides an incorrect answer. Examined the relationship between trust and user control. Explored scenarios that challenge user trust and included a final reflection.

Step 5. Final reflection: Reflected on how consistent, useful interactions can build reliance on AI over time. Documented how repeated use also revealed AI's limitations and potential to provide incorrect information.

imgs.title: Trust in AI: parameters of trust

sec.ev: Research steps, comparative examples, interaction flow, trust-versus-control exploration, and final reflection.

sec.head: 1.2 UX of AI Hallucinations
sec.sub: Comparative AI product research and UX exploration

sec.title: UX of AI Hallucinations
pts: Step 1. Initial understanding: Documented initial assumptions, understanding and opinions about AI hallucinations.
Step 2. Comparative analysis: Created a comparison table covering ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini.
Step 3. Response-state analysis: Explored how the platforms behave when answers are high-confidence, uncertain or incorrect.
Step 4. Confidence consequences: Investigated the UX implications of how AI communicates confidence and uncertainty.
Step 5. Interface exploration: Explored four interaction directions: collapse, challenge, verify and answer.
sec.ev: Initial assumptions, comparison table, example responses, confidence-state analysis, and the four interface directions.
